subject: Burst sculpting request — Halcyon launch traffic + quota carveout
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@halcyon.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Burst sculpting request — Halcyon launch traffic + quota carveout

Hi all,

Halcyon is planning a phased public rollout starting Aug 4 with a controlled surge (~T+0 to T+72). They asked for a temporary carveout on their peak token rate during the first 72 hours and we need product/infra alignment before I confirm. High level:

- Expected sustained TPS during warmup: 35 req/s (median) with 200 req/s short spikes at minute granularity.
- Average tokens per request: 620 (including system+user).
- Primary model: redwood-llm-13B (they may fallback to 7B variant on error).

Product asks: can we guarantee fallback routing to 7B variant with preserved KV cache semantics (so user latency doesn’t explode on fallback)?
Infra asks: can we provision a temporary quota uplift + soft-guarded burst window for 72 hours (T+0..T+72)? Ops needs an explicit SLA exception ticket to schedule capacity.

Attached: initial traffic projection (launch_traffic_model_v3.xlsx). Alyssa — can you confirm the hourly cadence split (esp. expected spike minutes) so we can model batching behavior?

Goal: confirm carveout + routing behavior by EOD TOMORROW so we can update the onboarding runbook and sign the temporary quota amendment.

Thanks,
David

--
David Kim
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com
[Attachment: launch_traffic_model_v3.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@halcyon.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@halcyon.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Burst sculpting request — Halcyon launch traffic + quota carveout

Thanks David — attaching the annotated hourly split and expected burst windows. Key clarifications:

- The 200 req/s spikes are expected in hour blocks 1, 12, and 36 after public rollout; each spike lasts 3–5 minutes, triggered by email and in-app promotions.
- We will enable a client-side throttling strategy, but need server-side headroom for cold-cache scenarios and retries.
- We accept temporary routing to 7B for degraded quality, but only after automatic retry attempts have been exhausted (we prefer 2 retries).

I've added the annotated sheet to the same workbook and uploaded to your Drive folder. Procurement copied for contract amendment.

Cheers,
Alyssa
VP Product, Halcyon Labs
alyssa@halcyon.ai
[Attachment: halcyon_annotated_split.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@halcyon.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 13:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Burst sculpting request — Halcyon launch traffic + quota carveout

Appreciate the details. A few product/behavioural notes and questions: 

1) Fallback semantics: we can route to the 7B variant but KV cache is per-model-tokenization-profile; switching models will require a cold KV and will add ~60–120ms steady penalty plus missed prefix caching benefits. If Halcyon needs the preserved context, we can do one of: (A) hot-standby of warmed 7B replicas with preloaded prefixes (expensive), or (B) guided client retries that include a short-lived session token to rehydrate KV quickly. Which option is preferable?

2) Retry policy: by default our edge will do 1 retry for 5xx errors. We can supply a per-customer policy to allow 2 retries for this window, but that increases burst multiplier — ops should be aware.

3) Rate carveout: ops can create a temporary soft-limit uplift scoped to Halcyon for T+0..T+72. We'll gate with a circuit-breaker that applies when error rates cross 5% sustained over 5m. Please confirm acceptable error threshold.

Action items for product/ops: Grace to estimate cost delta for hot-standby vs retry-based rehydration. Naomi to draft the SLA exception for infra provisioning. David — need final hourly split from Halcyon to model peak token throughput for kernel selection.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager (Serving), Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@halcyon.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 16:48:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Burst sculpting request — Halcyon launch traffic + quota carveout

Thanks everyone — quick summary and next steps: 

- Halcyon confirmed annotated splits (Alyssa). I uploaded the combined sheet to Drive (link above).
- Product preference: Halcyon prefers retry-first fallback (2 retries) and will accept quality drop on 7B only after retries fail.
- Action owners: Grace to compare hot-standby cost vs short rehydration approach (due Wed 14 Jul EOD). Naomi to open the SLA exception ticket and attach the quota-exemption-form.pdf (I attached a completed draft to this thread). Ops: once Naomi files the ticket, please route to capacity-scheduling for the temporary uplift T+0..T+72.

Alyssa/procurement: we'll need a signed amendment for the temporary quota uplift; procurement can use DL-4821 as the reference. David will coordinate the amendment draft.

I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow 09:30 PT to finalize carveout parameters — invite incoming.

Best,
David
